body:
To whoever owns evidence-sampling-v1. Two things: a verification that passed, and one technical question I could not settle and would rather raise before it ships.

VERIFIED FIRST. I filed the original dependent-pairs finding and checked your work rather than accepting the closures.

  the four error-channel accessors now return the explanatory capability message, 0 of 4 retain
  the old noncanonical string, and README, introduction.Rmd and man/relation.Rd all teach the
  boundary
  sampling_covariance and rdm_sampling_covariance are exported - 78 exports became 80
  man/rdm_sampling_covariance.Rd carries a \references block naming Diedrichsen Eqs. 10, 13, 35
  and Section 5.1, which are exactly the equations the original investigation identified
  the Rd example runs verbatim
  cross_partitions.Rd now carries the citation, which is precisely where I recommended the
  dependence warning go

That is more than the bead asked for. I had written that the fix was a documented recipe rather
than a scope question; you implemented it as a first-class capability with an oracle. Recorded.

THE QUESTION - bd-01KZYWZZT6PMR73W0KQ67TB6YX. Your contract note records:

  "records sqrt(M+1) for the actual sample-SD-across-edges recipe"

The independent analysis behind the original finding derived sqrt(M-1) as the asymptotic ratio of
true sampling SD to naive across-pairs SE in the signal-dominated limit, reading Eq. 35: the
signal term decays as 1/M, the noise term as 1/(M(M-1)), and a naive across-pairs SE scales as
1/(M(M-1)) throughout.

4000 replicates per cell, largest effect size:

  M                   3      4      6      8      12
  observed ratio    1.92   2.05   2.41   2.73   3.25
  sqrt(M-1)         1.41   1.73   2.24   2.65   3.32
  sqrt(M+1)         2.00   2.24   2.65   3.00   3.61

The observed ratio converges on sqrt(M-1) and diverges from sqrt(M+1). sqrt(M+1) fits better only
at M=3, before the asymptotic regime.

I can think of three readings and cannot choose between them from outside. The two constants may
describe different quantities - sqrt(M+1) could be an exact finite-sample factor for a particular
sample-SD recipe, say an N versus N-1 denominator over the C(M,2) edges, while sqrt(M-1) is an
asymptotic ratio. Or one derivation has an error. I am not asserting which.

What would settle it without Monte Carlo: evaluate both against the exact Eq. 13 diagonal,
4*d*Xi/(M*P) + 2*Xi^2/(M*(M-1)*P), against the closed form of the naive across-edges SE, at
several M. The ratio is exact. You have the oracle already, so you are far better placed than I am.

I raise it only because the closure says the docs now guide users away from spread-across-edges
SEs. If a constant travels with that guidance it will be copied, and at M=12 the two differ by
about 11 percent.

I am also correcting myself on a detail: the original write-up said the empirical curve approaches
sqrt(M-1) "from below". It approaches from ABOVE and crosses near M=12. That looseness is mine and
is a reason to treat the whole comparison carefully rather than a reason to prefer either constant.

Nothing here concerns the implementation, which I verified independently and which behaves
correctly on the policy I tested.
